item.title: Decode One Instruction: CALL rel32 (Windows x86-64)
item.description:
A disassembler shows raw bytes at address 0x140001005 inside a function:
0x140001005: E8 D6 0F 00 00
Decode this single instruction: name the opcode, the addressing form of its operand, and compute the exact target address it transfers control to.
Answer: call 0x140001FE0
- E8 is the opcode for CALL rel32 (near, direct call) - a one-byte opcode followed by a 4-byte little-endian signed displacement, no ModRM byte at all since the target is instruction-pointer-relative rather than register/memory. - The displacement bytes D6 0F 00 00 read little-endian as 0x00000FD6 (4054); RIP-relative encodings are always computed from the address of the next instruction, not the CALL's own start. - Next instruction address = 0x140001005 + 5 (opcode + 4 displacement bytes) = 0x14000100A; adding the displacement gives 0x14000100A + 0xFD6 = 0x140001FE0, and executing CALL also pushes the return address 0x14000100A onto the stack before jumping.
